<reason>CON won the live comparison after both sides accepted caps and housing rules: remaining demand need not be shared, because relief tracks actual pressure and extra service costs, not a district’s share of sightseeing. PRO was punchier on fairness and boom-bust, but never escaped the double standard of treating regulation as protection only when tourism is spread, so CON left the cleaner reason to reject the motion.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s reply that a high share of a genuinely smaller cap is not still a crush, and that PRO cannot count licensing as sufficient only in newly promoted neighborhoods.</best_rebuttal>
